summary: The read-only kernel's disk diagnostic, reached over SSH with nothing typed at the console, reports a drive and hands out its sectors without writing a byte, and reports a missing drive; the program is tests/cases/machine/diskdiag_scenario.c

cases.behavior: a boot of the read-write kernel mounts the disk and changes it; the read-only kernel's diagnostic, over SSH once init has started the server, reports the drive, its size and its table in /proc/disk, gives each sector the disk has, issues no command its allowlist refuses and leaves its copy of the disk byte for byte; and with no drive it says that none answered

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machines and removes the two copies of the disk and the copy of the demo key, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the declared Rach2 OpenSSH client and open its framed command channel
boot the read-write kernel on a copy of the disk to its debug shell, end it with QMP's quit, and compare the copy with the disk

boot the read-only kernel on another copy of the disk on AHCI, wait for init to start the SSH server, read /proc/disk and three sectors over SSH, try a write, end it with QMP's quit, and compare the copy with the disk
boot the read-only kernel with no drive to its debug shell and end it with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the read-write kernel says krffs: mounted: before its debug shell greets
the read-write boot leaves its copy different from the disk, since the mount sets the dirty flag; without it the diagnostic's comparison could not find a write
after init says it started the SSH server, the machine runs a command for root by the demo key, tried again only while ssh fails
/proc/disk says state present, driver ahci, policy read-only, mounted 0 and mbr-signature ok, each a line of its own
/proc/disk gives the disk's size in sectors, the host's size of the disk over 512, so that a wrong IDENTIFY cannot agree with a number written into the test
sector 0 read through /dev/disk0 has the SHA-256 of the disk's sector 0 on the host
sector 2048, the partition's first, read through /dev/disk0 has the SHA-256 of the disk's sector 2048 on the host
the disk's last sector read through /dev/disk0 has the SHA-256 of that sector on the host
a write to /dev/disk0 is refused above the driver: the kernel never says refused: command
the diagnostic boot leaves its copy byte for byte the disk
with no drive the kernel says diskdiag: absent: no disk answered

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the proof that the diagnostic writes nothing is the disk's bytes after the boot, read off a copy the host compares, and the absent drive needs a machine with none
